title: Anthropic signs $11.6bn Akamai cloud deal and gets warrant for 5% of Akamai
excerpt: Anthropic has signed an $11.6bn, seven-year cloud infrastructure deal with Akamai, with an option to expand to roughly $20bn. As part of the agreement, Akamai...
content_html:
Anthropic has signed an $11.6bn, seven-year cloud infrastructure deal with Akamai, with an option to expand to roughly $20bn. As part of the agreement, Akamai issued Anthropic a warrant for 7.7 million shares (about 5% of common stock), the first such warrant Akamai has given a customer. Akamai will supply CPU access and expects to spend about $5.5bn in capital to fulfill the contract, raising 2026 capex by $1.7bn. Revenue from Anthropic is projected at $150-300m next year, rising to a $1.7bn annual run rate by 2028. The deal builds on a $1.8bn agreement signed in May and adds to a string of large compute deals Anthropic has made this year, including with Volta and Rum Group.

How much is Anthropic's cloud deal with Akamai worth?

Anthropic signed an $11.6 billion, seven-year agreement for Akamai's cloud infrastructure, with the potential to expand by another $9 billion to reach about $20 billion total. Akamai will supply CPU access, and the deal builds on a prior $1.8 billion agreement the companies signed in May. Akamai expects to spend roughly $5.5 billion in capital to serve the contract. Track how large AI compute deals like this one on daily.dev reshape cloud infrastructure spending.

What is the Akamai warrant given to Anthropic in their cloud deal?

Akamai issued Anthropic a warrant for 7.7 million shares on an as-converted basis, roughly 5% of its common stock, at an exercise price of $111.33, in the form of non-voting convertible Series B preferred stock. About 2% vests immediately with the $11.6 billion commitment, while the remaining 3% vests only if the contract expands, at 1% per $3 billion of additional services. This marks the first time Akamai has given a customer a warrant in a cloud deal. Follow evolving vendor-customer equity arrangements in AI cloud deals on daily.dev.

How much revenue does Akamai expect from its Anthropic deal by 2028?

Akamai's CEO Tom Leighton projects $150 million to $300 million in revenue from Anthropic in the first year after the contract starts in the second half of next year, rising to an annual run rate of about $1.7 billion by 2028. Akamai is raising its 2026 capital spending by about $1.7 billion to pre-buy supplies including memory for the contract.
